questions: Can we swap any two positions where one holds value a and the other holds value b, regardless of whether they are from the same couple or not, or must we swap exactly one a with one b each time?
Are we allowed to swap positions where the values are the same (e.g., two a's) as part of the process to achieve adjacency, or are swaps restricted only to pairs (a, b) as described?
Does the operation need to be performed exactly as described (swapping a and b) each time, or can we also swap other pairs of values (like a and c) to facilitate the adjacency condition?

When we say 'by performing the following operation one or more times in any order', does that mean we can only use swaps between a and b, or can we also use swaps that involve other couples as long as the final state satisfies adjacency for a and b?
Is the goal to achieve a state where both couples a and b are adjacent simultaneously, or is it sufficient to achieve adjacency for a and b in separate states (i.e., one after another)?

Do we consider the swaps to be performed on the original sequence A, or can we consider any sequence reachable by swapping a and b multiple times, possibly involving intermediate states where a or b become adjacent before the final state?
Are we allowed to swap the same pair of positions multiple times (e.g., swap back and forth) as part of the sequence of operations?
Does the operation require that i and j be distinct positions, and if so, is there any restriction on their relative order or distance in the sequence?
